prerequisites: Having taken the courses Elasticity and Strength of Materials I and II and Calculation and Design of Structures.
Having passed the courses Elasticity and Strength of Materials I and II and Calculation and Design of Structures.
Active class attendance and resolution of proposed exercises.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability, given the initial hypotheses, to establish the structural model in each case, the resistant scheme, and the basic parameters of the structure (type of material, structural elements, actions to resist, types of support, etc.) for obtaining forces and displacements.
Ability to understand the meaning and scope of the fundamental principles and initial hypotheses to know the limitations of the model.
Ability to apply the basic equations of structural calculation (compatibility, equilibrium, and behavior) in an organized manner and to use common computer tools in structural calculation.
Ability to use a finite element program for the linear calculation of simple bar, plate, and shell structures.
Decision-making ability regarding the validity of the results obtained.

syllabus_topics: Load determination. Combinations. Wind and earthquake
Structure of a technical report. Structural drawings. Site agents. Responsibilities
teaching_methods: Development of matrix calculation and finite element programs
Use of commercial software for analysis and problem-solving
Tutorials (in-person or virtual, individual or group)

assessment_methods.method: Final in-person exam to evaluate overall learning of the course
Written/computer-based assignments presented on different course contents, performed individually and in groups
Oral presentation of the assignments carried out during the course
Report on the computer practicals performed on structural calculation learning

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a final in-person exam (20%), written/computer-based assignments (50%), an oral presentation of assignments (10%), and a report on computer practicals (20%). The practicals are mandatory. Assignments will be evaluated using rubrics and partial submissions with possibilities for improvement. The value of each proposed exercise in the final exam will be indicated. The report on computer practicals will be assessed through a documentary analysis of the work performed.
